subject: DPA: training-data carve-outs, subprocessors, and DocuSign flow with EdgeBank
messages:
From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@edgebank.com>

Cc: procurement@edgebank.com
Date: Mon, 2 Jun 2025 17:12:00 +0000
Subject: EdgeBank DPA redline + training carve-out

Vanessa —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our redline of Redwood's standard DPA (EdgeBank_DPA_Redline_v2.docx). High-level items we'd like you to consider before we route for final sign-off:

- A clear carve-out that prohibits the use of EdgeBank customer data to train or improve models without an explicit, opt-in program and separate commercial terms. We inserted proposed language in Section 3.4.
- Subprocessors: please confirm current list and whether you will notify before onboarding any new subprocessor handling personal data.
- International transfers: we need to confirm mechanisms for EU-origin data. SCCs are preferred; are you able to commit to SCCs or equivalent?
- Audit evidence: SOC 2 type II report and encryption-in-transit details.

We're aiming to complete by the end of the week if possible. Procurement has asked for a DocuSign envelope when you have an executed version.

Emily Ross
Senior Counsel, EdgeBank
legal@edgebank.com

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: EdgeBank DPA redline + training carve-out

Emily — thanks for the thorough redline. I reviewed the doc this morning and looped in legal (Markus) and our sales lead (Kim) to get procurement details aligned. Quick notes: 

- We can commit to a strict "no training" default: Redwood will not use EdgeBank data to train, fine-tune, or improve models unless there is an express, written opt-in program that includes scope, duration, and compensation. I asked Markus to draft a one-sentence carve-out that is narrow and maps to your suggested Section 3.4 phrasing.
- Subprocessors: we keep an updated list and will notify customers 30 days before onboarding new subprocessors that will process personal data. We will attach our current subprocessor CSV; IT will confirm whether any planned changes are imminent.
- Transfers: Redwood supports SCCs and can execute them for EU-to-US transfers. We also have a contractual commitment in our DPA template to rely on SCCs where required.
- Evidence: we can provide a recent SOC 2 Type II report and a whitepaper on our encryption practices.

We're preparing a redline back and expect to upload it tonight. If these high-level positions work, we can prepare an executed DocuSign envelope for EdgeBank procurement.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
(Attachment) RBW_Subprocessor_List_20250603.csv
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Jun 2025 14:28:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: EdgeBank DPA redline + proposed language

Folks — I'm dropping the proposed carve-out language below and my suggested tweaks to Section 3.4. Markus, can you weigh in on the legal precision? Kim, if you could prepare a short note on commercial implications if EdgeBank insists on an opt-in training addendum (pricing/term impact), that would help procurement move quicker.

Proposed insertion (for discussion):
"Customer Data will not be used to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve machine learning models or algorithmic systems operated by Redwood Inference, except where Customer provides an explicit, documented opt-in specifying the scope, data categories, retention period, and compensation. For clarity, aggregated or anonymized derivatives that are not reasonably re-identifiable are not considered Customer Data for the purposes of this restriction."

Suggested change: remove the parentheses around "aggregation" clause and change "not reasonably re-identifiable" to "irreversibly anonymized in accordance with NIST SP 800-188 guidelines". That helps with legal clarity while leaving a narrow path for safe aggregated analytics.

Also attached: an internal checklist I'd like security to confirm (SOC 2 doc, encryption endpoints, data residency controls).

Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Emily Ross <emily.ross@edgebank.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@edgebank.com, legal@edgebank.com
Date: Wed, 4 Jun 2025 15:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: EdgeBank DPA redline + training carve-out

Vanessa/Rishi — appreciate the quick turnaround and proposed language. Two points from our side: 

1) The anonymization standard: EdgeBank legal is comfortable with referencing a recognized standard but prefers the language to be "irreversibly de-identified in accordance with commonly accepted industry standards (e.g., NIST, ISO)." We don't require a single spec but want to avoid a vendor-specific interpretation.

2) Subprocessors and notification: 30 days notice is acceptable; however, we request the right to object to any new subprocessor that will have access to unredacted Customer Data. Objections would be reasonable if there is a documented security/regulatory concern.

Procurement also asked: once we have an agreed final DPA, can Redwood send a DocuSign envelope to procurement@edgebank.com and copy legal for signature? Please include a copy to Vanessa for countersignature.

If you can include SOC 2 and encryption notes as attachments to the envelope, that would expedite our internal risk review.

Thanks —
Emily
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Emily Ross <emily.ross@edgebank.com>, procurement@edgebank.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Jun 2025 23:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: EdgeBank DPA redline + training carve-out

Emily —

Thanks — all good on our side. Summary of agreed positions: 

- Training carve-out: Redwood confirms default prohibition on using Customer Data to train or improve models unless EdgeBank provides an explicit written opt-in addendum that defines scope, duration, data categories, and commercial terms. We will adopt the agreed anonymization language: "irreversibly de-identified in accordance with commonly accepted industry standards (e.g., NIST, ISO)."
- Subprocessors: Redwood will provide current list and 30 days notice for additions. EdgeBank may object to a new subprocessor that would access unredacted Customer Data on documented security/regulatory grounds; we will include an objection path in the DPA.
- Transfers: Redwood will include SCCs for EU data flows and will attach SOC 2 Type II and encryption whitepaper to the DocuSign envelope.

I've uploaded our clean DPA with the agreed language and started a DocuSign envelope. Link: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/status/0a1b2c3d4e5f

Attachments included in envelope: SOC2_TypeII_Redwood_202504.pdf, Encryption_Whitepaper_202503.pdf, Final_DPA_EdgeBank_RBW-4921.docx

Emily — once procurement confirms this envelope is acceptable, we'll proceed to signature. Kim will follow up on commercial addendum options if EdgeBank wants an opt-in training program later.

Best regards,
